## 8. POST-GEN NOTES
- Tight prompt: a short Style field (a scene, a tempo feel, a key colour, the lead, one lateness phrase) and three to five short section tags, following the 2026-11 research (research/07). Judge it on four or more takes: one take tells you less than the difference between two takes of the same prompt. The Detailed switch writes the long version of the same roll.
- Structure: the first full beat lands at about 0:10; the layout is "False start: two bars, dead silence, then the beat for real" and runs about 2:55. Straight mode: the same drums in every section, hard cuts only.
- Attitude: rise ("remembering, a little sad and glad at once"). Hopeful and motivating: the key leans major, the riff climbs, the drums hit hard under a sweet sample. If it comes back dark, re-roll.
- The mystery ingredient (the hatless bars) appears once, in the last hook: it is meant to be barely there and to send the track over the edge once. If Suno makes it constant, lower Style Influence five points; if it is missing, that is acceptable on a first take.
- No hint on this roll; the hook device in the lead line ("the melody circles the fifth and never lands on the root until the last bar") carries the stickiness. Listen for it on the second pass.
- It should feel like a win: a sample or horn riff that climbs, a major-leaning key, drums that hit hard. If it comes back dark or moody, re-roll; the lane bans every dark word.
- The sample is an instrument here, never a sung line. Any sung or spoken phrase means a re-roll.
- Big drums under a sweet sample is the whole trick: if the drums come back soft, raise Style Influence five points.
- Fills, risers or a roll at a section change mean a word slipped through: run the QA checker on the block, and keep the anti-transition phrase in the drums line (it is the positive form of "no fills").
- Any hum, chant or sung syllable means a re-roll, not a fix: the Exclude list is already complete, so change the seed rather than adding words.
- Ending: [End] should stop it near 2:55. If it runs on, Crop to the last downbeat. If it stops early, Extend from the last good section and paste only the remaining section tags.
- Extend when the first 60-90 s are keepers and only the back half drifts. Re-roll (or run the weirder variation on v6-wild) when the drums or the lead are wrong from the start.
- Remaster: Remaster (Pro/Premier) renders subtle variations and runs on v6; use it on the keeper for a cleaner, louder master.
- Stems: Get Stems (Pro/Premier): Auto Split up to 12 stems for 50 credits; Split from Mix 10 credits per stem; Advanced Split (choose from ~100 instruments) 10 credits per stem, Premier only.
- Prompt ignored? Check Variety is Off (v6 defaults it to Normal, which rewrites the Style text) and Max Mode is on. Then check Style Influence is 70 or higher.
